first_impression.reaction: Googled 'santorini wedding packages' with two Santorini quotes open in another tab. The first line says what I already suspected: same word, different product. No sunsets-over-the-caldera fluff, and no 'book now' in the takeaways. I went to the FAQ first, then 'What packages often leave out', then the checklist. It names venues, hours, decibel limits, room minimums and deposit terms. That's what I came for. My niggles: the planner option is the only one with no downside, a couple of FAQ answers wander off, and a few venues get a mention without telling me anything I can compare.

journey.quote: Santorini wedding packages share a name and very little else.
journey.reaction: Good. That's my problem in one line, and nobody's selling me anything yet.

journey.quote: Several Santorini venues require a wedding planner on top of the venue fee, which changes what a package is really worth to you.
journey.reaction: Handy thing for a planning company to tell me. But they name Grace Hotel and Santorini Gem further down, so I can check it myself. Fine.

journey.quote: Compare quotes on the same guest count, spaces, hours, nights, music times and currency before paying a deposit that may not be refundable.
journey.reaction: Takeaways with no booking link in them. The first ask isn't until after the evidence. That's the right order.

journey.section: Reception, menus and drinks where the venue states them
journey.quote: Open bar packages are optional, but once chosen they apply to every adult guest.
journey.reaction: That's the sort of catch I'd only find buried in a PDF. Pointed out plainly.

journey.quote: Grand Ambassador Santorini offers Wedding and Honeymoon Packages that include champagne and strawberries on arrival, candlelit dinners and couples' massages, along with a private photo session at a pool of your choice where available.
journey.reaction: Honeymoon extras. Doesn't help me compare a wedding quote. Skimmed it.

journey.section: Small wedding packages up to around 50 guests
journey.quote: Kivotos Santorini names three packages, The Dreamy Life, The Live Life and The Get Together, with inclusions on request.
journey.reaction: Three package names and nothing in them. Same with Katikies further up. It's filler next to the Canaves and Gem detail.

journey.quote: At Canaves Epitome, the room requirement grows with the guest list: one room for three nights for 8 to 25 guests, three rooms for 26 to 45, then four or six rooms, a half buyout of 25 rooms for 80 to 100 guests and a full buyout of 53 rooms above 100, each with a three-night minimum.
journey.reaction: Hard numbers on the condition that would actually blow my budget. This is proof, not promises.

journey.quote: At Santorini Gem, music runs up to 80 dB, is lowered to listening level at 11pm and switched off 15 minutes before the end time, and the bar closes 30 minutes before the end.
journey.reaction: Specific. That 1.30am finish isn't really 1.30am, and they tell you so.

journey.section: Venue package, venue fee or a planner
journey.quote: A planner connects the venue, suppliers and guests into one plan, and is the route several Santorini venues insist on.
journey.reaction: The package gets a downside (fixed inclusions, venue's suppliers). The venue fee gets a downside (you need a planner and separate costings). The planner, which is what you sell, gets none. That's exactly where I notice whose website this is.

journey.section: How to compare two Santorini quotes like for like
journey.quote: Canaves states that its deposit is non-refundable, that the balance is due one month before the event, and that venue payments are always non-refundable.
journey.reaction: Real terms from a real venue, inside the checklist. The whole list is going into my spreadsheet.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller says some countries ask you to prove you are free to marry, most often with a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) and certificates from a registry of births, deaths and marriages.
journey.reaction: Dated, and it names the government source. I can check that in thirty seconds.

journey.section: For Australian couples: currency, deposits and insurance
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and confirms every inclusion in writing before you commit, so you can book a Wedded Concierge consultation with both quotes in hand.
journey.reaction: The CTA comes after the evidence, so fair enough. But two lines earlier you asked me 'who carries that risk?' on exchange rates, and then you quote in AUD. So who carries it with you? I'd ask that on the call.

journey.quote: Rarely. A package covers what its list names.
journey.reaction: Straight answer, then named exclusions behind it. That's what an FAQ is for.

journey.quote: Grace Hotel sets its venue fee inclusions either side of 50 guests, and Canaves Epitome has packages for 26 to 45 and 45 to 100 guests.
journey.reaction: The body gave me 26 to 45 and then rooms for 80 to 100. I didn't see a 45 to 100 package up there, and 45 is in both bands. I scrolled back up to check and couldn't match it.

journey.quote: Vedema's wine cellar holds up to 120 for a banquet and 150 for a reception.
journey.reaction: The question is whether a package works for about 50. A wine cellar for 150 isn't an answer, and Vedema's package isn't described anywhere in the article.

journey.quote: Yes. Venues such as Andronis and Canaves offer legal ceremonies, and a marriage valid where it took place, and valid under Australian law, is in most cases recognised in Australia.

unanswered_questions: Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or mark-up from any of these Santorini venues, and does that affect which ones get recommended?
How is the Wedded Concierge fee worked out, and what does it buy on top of a venue's in-house planner?
When the Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD, whose exchange rate is used and who carries the currency risk between deposit and balance?
Is the first consultation free, and what do I walk away with?
Is the Canaves Epitome package for 45 to 100 guests a separate package, and what does it include?
Is there a real Santorini wedding with the actual budget I can look at?

turn_offs_found.quote: A planner connects the venue, suppliers and guests into one plan, and is the route several Santorini venues insist on.
turn_offs_found.why: The other two options each get an honest catch in the same list. The one the business sells gets only an upside. That one-sidedness undercuts the balance of everything around it, and it's the line I'd quote back to a planner on Reddit.

turn_offs_found.quote: If you would rather start from a package that has been curated end to end, browse our curated destination wedding packages and read what each one lists against the same questions.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Curated end to end' is marketing talk dropped straight after a section about how packages hide what they don't include. To be fair, the second half tells me to test them against the same questions, which softens it. Mild.

would_share_with: My fiancee, the quote checklist, to send to both Santorini venues
My dad, the currency, deposit and insurance section

cta_reaction.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD for Australian couples and confirms every inclusion in writing before you commit, so you can book a Wedded Concierge consultation with both quotes in hand.
cta_reaction.why: The page earned the ask. It comes after the evidence, it's tied to the thing I actually have (two quotes), and 'in writing' is the right promise. What stops a straight yes is the question I ask every planner: do you take a cut from the venue, and is there a margin in the AUD quote? The planner option being the only one with no downside makes me a bit more careful.

top_3_changes: Give the planner bullet in 'Venue package, venue fee or a planner' an honest trade-off, like the other two get (for example, it's another party and another fee to agree), so the section doesn't read as one-sided.

Fix the 'around 50 guests' FAQ: make the Canaves Epitome bands match the body (the body shows 26 to 45, not a 45 to 100 package, and 45 sits in both bands), and swap the Vedema wine cellar line for one that answers the package question.

Trim the mentions that give me nothing to compare (Kivotos package names, Katikies micro weddings, Grand Ambassador honeymoon extras) or cut them down to one line, so the detailed venues stand out. (Commission, fee model and AUD margin would help me enquire, but those are deferred business details, so nice-to-have.)

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ and exclusions first, looked for catches, one-sided claims, fee model and currency risk
No invented brand facts; commission, fee, AUD conversion and first-call details placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (image slots, fact tags, CTA marker) ignored
Title, deferred business details and absence of prices not flagged as must-fix; no requests for sourcing or 'not published' explanations

open_questions.question: The planner bullet is the only option with no trade-off. That's a copy-balance fix, not a fee disclosure. Should the writer add one this round?

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'santorini wedding packages' holding two Santorini quotes, hence top relevance.
No prices on the page is by design and not penalised.
Title is person-set and deferred, so not assessed.
